'''O Clássico''' ({{lit|The Classic}}) is the name given in [[Association football|football]] to matches between Portuguese clubs [[S.L. Benfica]] and [[FC Porto]]. Originally, the term ''O Clássico'' only referred to games played in the [[Primeira Liga|league]], but now tends to include matches that take place in other domestic competitions such as the [[Taça de Portugal]], [[Taça da Liga]] and [[Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira]]. Despite being the two most decorated Portuguese clubs in [[European football]], with seven European trophies between them, they have never faced each other in a European competition. Benfica and Porto are two of the three clubs known as the "[[Big Three (Portugal)|Big Three]]" in Portugal, the other being [[Sporting CP]].

The rivalry comes about as [[Lisbon]] and [[Porto]] are the two largest cities in [[Portugal]], and both clubs are the most decorated football teams in Portugal.

== Rivalry ==
[[File:Matraquilhos Benfica-Porto.jpg|thumbnail|right|A [[table football|fuzboll]] table depicting the rivalry between Benfica and Porto]]
[[File:The Da Luz Stadium before a game between SL Benfica and FC Porto.jpg|thumb|''O Clássico'' at [[Estádio da Luz]] on 7 October 2018]]
The first match between the ''Águias'' and the ''Dragões'' was an [[exhibition game]] that was played on the 28 April 1912, when Benfica defeated Porto 8–2.<ref name="BenficaVsPorto">{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/clubs/rivalries/newsid=1015039/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121219024321/http://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/clubs/rivalries/newsid=1015039/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 December 2012|title=RIVALRIES Benfica Vs Porto Portugal's great divide|work=[[FIFA]]|access-date=18 February 2013}}</ref> Eight years later, Porto would win their first ''Clássico'', 3–2. Porto would have to wait another nine years to accumulate their second victory over Benfica. Prior to the establishment of the [[Primeira Liga]] in 1934, both Benfica and Porto were competing within their football league district. Both sides were also competing in the [[Taça de Portugal#Campeonato de Portugal|Campeonato de Portugal]] which later became in 1938 the [[Taça de Portugal]].

Until 1934, Benfica would win the [[Campeonato de Lisboa]] nine times as well as triumphing in the [[Taça de Honra]] de Lisboa twice, while Porto would win the Campeonato do Porto nineteen times as well as claiming the Taça de Honra do Porto twice. Benfica would meet Porto for the first time in an official match in the domestic cup competition which during the early periods of Portuguese football was the Campeonato de Portugal. Benfica defeated Porto in the final of the 1931 Campeonato de Portugal, 3–0 at the Campo do Arnado in [[Coimbra]]. Two goals from [[Vítor Silva]] and one from Augusto Dinis sealed the win to claim Benfica's second Campeonato de Portugal.{{citation needed|date=October 2025}}

The inception of the [[Primeira Liga]] saw Porto win the very [[1934–35 Primeira Liga|first edition of the competition]].{{citation needed|date=October 2025}} Both sides met for the first time in the competition on 3 February 1935, on which Porto won 2–1.{{citation needed|date=October 2025}} Benfica would win the return tie 3–0. Despite Benfica's win, the ''Águias'' would finish third in the league, three points behind Porto.{{citation needed|date=October 2025}} The next five seasons would see Benfica win three titles to Porto's two. During the 1940s, both sides would take a back seat to [[Sporting CP]], which would win five league titles in the decade.

The late 1950s and 1960s saw Benfica dominate not just Portuguese football but also European football. The arrival of [[Eusébio]] saw Benfica secure eight league titles in ten years.<ref name="BenficaVsPorto" /> Benfica's league titles were joined by two consecutive [[European Champion Clubs' Cup|European Cups]] which were won in [[1960–61 European Cup#Final|1961]], 3–2 against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], and in [[1961–62 European Cup#Final|1962]], 5–3 against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]. The 1970s saw the continuation of Benfica's dominance up until the [[1977–78 Primeira Divisão|1977–78 season]], during which Porto won the league title for the first time in 19 years. The 1980s and early 1990s saw both Benfica and Porto battle for the league title. Porto's resurgence and the introduction of [[Jorge Nuno Pinto da Costa]] as chairman saw Porto reach new heights, winning the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] for the first time after defeating [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] 2–1 in the [[1987 European Cup Final]].<ref name="BenficaVsPorto" /> Three years later, Benfica reached their eighth European final, the [[1990 European Cup Final]], losing 1–0 to [[A.C. Milan|Milan]].

In the 1990s, Porto began to dominate Portuguese football, winning a record five consecutive league titles.<ref name="BenficaVsPorto" /> The intensity between these two sides in the '90s was culminated by the fact that former [[Portugal national football team|Portuguese international]] teammates [[João Pinto]], who played for Benfica, and [[Paulinho Santos]], who played for Porto, publicly declared their dislike for each other. The new millennium saw a continuation of Porto's dominance.<ref name="BenficaVsPorto" /> Porto would reach the heights of their 1987 European Cup final win after [[José Mourinho]] guided ''Os Dragões'' to the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] in [[2003 UEFA Cup Final|2003]] and the UEFA Champions League in [[2004 UEFA Champions League Final|2004]]. Benfica won the league title in 2005 for the first time in over ten years to halter Porto's momentum. During the second half of the 2000s, both sides battled for top spot, with the rivalry intensified after Benfica's [[Cristian Rodríguez]] joined Porto in the summer of 2008 to become the third Benfica player in recent history to have made the switch. In 2010, after four seasons, Benfica won their 32nd league title. Also in 2010, Benfica defeated Porto 3–0 in the [[2009–10 Taça da Liga#Final|2009–10 Taça da Liga final]] to win the first of what would be four straight Taça da Liga titles, a competition that Porto would only win in the [[2022–23 Taça da Liga#Final|2022–23 edition]] against Sporting CP.

The next year, Porto recorded their biggest home win over ''As Águias'', a 5–0 thrashing in a league fixture.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.zerozero.pt/noticia.php?id=21789|title=Goleada no clássico e caminho aberto para o título|trans-title=Thrashing at the clássico and a clear opening to the title|work=ZeroZero|language=pt|date=7 November 2010|access-date=20 February 2013}}</ref> Porto would secure a treble in the same season in which they claimed the league title, the Taça de Portugal as well as the UEFA Europa League.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.zerozero.pt/noticia.php?id=28351|title=Golo à Falcao dá Liga Europa ao FC Porto|trans-title=Goal from Falcao gives Europa League to FC Porto|work=ZeroZero|language=pt|date=18 May 2011|access-date=20 February 2013}}</ref> On 18 May 2014, Benfica made history after achieving the domestic treble of winning the [[2013–14 Primeira Liga|Primeira Liga]], [[2013–14 Taça de Portugal|Taça de Portugal]] and [[2013–14 Taça da Liga|Taça da Liga]]. Later on, Benfica secured four more league titles – four in a row and 37 overall, the latter a Portuguese record – and won another two league cups, achieving a record seventh overall. Porto and Benfica would go back-and-forth as league champions from the [[2017–18 Primeira Liga|2017–18 season]] through to the [[2019–20 Primeira Liga|2019–20 season]].

== Campeonato de Portugal matches ==
The matches listed below are only [[Taça de Portugal#Campeonato de Portugal|Campeonato de Portugal]] matches. The Campeonato de Portugal was created in 1922 and was the primary tournament in Portugal, where all teams competed from around the country. In 1938, the Campeonato de Portugal became what is now known as the [[Taça de Portugal]]. The club name in '''bold''' indicates win. The score is given at full-time and half-time (in brackets), and in the goals columns, the goalscorer and time when goal was scored is noted.{{citation needed|date=October 2025}}

== Reserve team matches ==
Both Benfica's reserves, [[S.L. Benfica B|Benfica B]], and Porto's reserves, [[FC Porto B|Porto B]], were established in the late 1990s. Both sides folded following the end of the 2005–06 season. The two teams were re-established in 2012 to compete in the [[2012–13 Segunda Liga]], where they met for the first time.

== Records and statistics ==
[[File:Porto - Benfica Graph.jpg|thumb|right|400px|Chart showing the finishing league positions of Benfica (red) and Porto (blue) between the 1934–35 and 2009–10 seasons]]
* '''Biggest Benfica home win:''' Benfica 12–2 Porto (7 February 1943){{citation needed|date=October 2025}}
* '''Biggest Benfica away win:''' Porto 2–8 Benfica (28 May 1952, in the inauguration of Porto's [[Estádio das Antas]])
* '''Most consecutive Benfica wins:''' 4 (12 September 1971 – 5 November 1972){{citation needed|date=October 2025}}
* '''Longest undefeated Benfica run:''' 7 (24 January 1982 – 8 December 1983){{citation needed|date=October 2025}}
* '''Most consecutive Benfica losses:''' 4 (10 February 2002 – 21 September 2003, 24 August 2019 – 23 December 2020){{citation needed|date=October 2025}}
* '''Most consecutive matches without Benfica winning:''' 9 (31 January 1988 – 17 April 1991){{citation needed|date=October 2025}}
* '''Biggest Porto home win:''' Porto 8–0 Benfica (28 May 1933){{citation needed|date=October 2025}}
* '''Biggest Porto away win:''' Benfica 0–5 Porto (18 September 1996){{citation needed|date=October 2025}}
* '''Most consecutive Porto wins:''' 4 (10 February 2002 – 21 September 2003, 24 August 2019 – 23 December 2020){{citation needed|date=October 2025}}
* '''Longest undefeated Porto run:''' 9 (31 January 1988 – 17 April 1991)<ref name="Red card">{{cite news|date=23 December 2021|url=https://www.zerozero.pt/news.php?id=346598|title=Otamendi faz história (pela negativa) frente a um dragão dominante em Clássicos|work=zerozero|language=pt|access-date=24 December 2021}}</ref>{{citation needed|date=October 2025}}
* '''Most consecutive Porto losses:''' 4 (12 September 1971 – 5 November 1972){{citation needed|date=October 2025}}
* '''Most consecutive matches without Porto winning:''' 7 (24 January 1982 – 8 December 1983){{citation needed|date=October 2025}}
* '''Most common result:''' 1–1 (14 times){{citation needed|date=October 2025}}

Sergei Yuran, Maxi Pereira, and Nicolás Otamendi are the only players who have scored a goal for both sides in ''O Clássico''.<ref>{{cite news|date=2 April 2017|url=https://www.ojogo.pt/futebol/1a-liga/porto/noticias/interior/maxi-fez-o-que-so-yuran-tinha-conseguido-5765725.html|title=Maxi fez o que só Yuran tinha conseguido|language=pt|trans-title=Maxi did what only Yuran had achieved|website=[[O Jogo]]|access-date=17 July 2017}}</ref> Otamendi is the only player to have been sent off for both clubs.<ref name="Red card"/>
